findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime sort keys
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies Paginator.get_item_key, which does `int(math.floor(value))` on the item's sort-key attribute. The only caller of this class (organization_auditlogs.py) paginates with order_by="-datetime", so `value` is a `datetime` and `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError. DateTimePaginator exists precisely to convert datetimes to epoch-ms; the optimized class also lacks DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor's ms-to-datetime conversion, so a page-2 cursor would compare a timestamp column against a raw float in SQL. Net effect: any request with `optimized_pagination=true` will 500 (page 1 in get_item_key via build_cursor, page 2+ in the where clause).

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing of a Django QuerySet raises AssertionError
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is on and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySet slicing explicitly rejects negative indices ("AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported"), so this path raises instead of paginating. The inline comments ("The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically", "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level") are factually wrong: negative slicing does not work on querysets, and permissions have nothing to do with slicing. The advertised core feature of this paginator cannot function as written.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features kwarg is not accepted by Endpoint.paginate
findings.body: The endpoint calls `self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True)`, but `Endpoint.paginate` in sentry/api/base.py has a fixed keyword signature (paginator_cls, order_by, on_results, max_limit, desc, count_hits, known_hits, max_hits) and constructs the paginator with only those arguments — it does not forward arbitrary kwargs to `paginator_cls`. Unless the base method was also changed (it is not in this PR), this call raises `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`, 500-ing every request that passes `optimized_pagination=true` with the required privileges. Even if the intent is for the flag to reach the paginator, `BasePaginator.__init__` would then need to receive it.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the endpoint's optimized branch
findings.body: The PR adds ~100 lines of new paginator code (OptimizedCursorPaginator), modifies BasePaginator.get_result's offset handling for every existing paginator, and adds a new request-driven code path to the audit logs endpoint, yet includes zero tests: no unit tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator (including its negative-offset branch), no tests that BasePaginator behavior is unchanged for existing paginators, and no endpoint tests for the `optimized_pagination` parameter (including the authorization gate). Any of the crash modes described in the other findings would have been caught by a single basic test invoking the new code path.

findings.title: Unrelated audit-log pagination feature mixed into a span-buffer PR with no rationale
findings.body: This PR is titled "Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert" and its description is just "Test 2", yet roughly half the diff introduces an unrelated, undocumented API behavior (`optimized_pagination=true` query param enabling a different paginator for superusers/global-access members) to the audit logs endpoint. This makes the change unreviewable as a unit and unrollbackable independently: a revert of the span-buffer work would either take the API change with it or require manual surgery. The audit-log changes should be split into their own PR with a real description, and if kept, the new query param should be documented/validated rather than read ad-hoc from request.GET.

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000, splitting deep segments
findings.body: The redirect-following loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations, and the comment explaining the tradeoff ("theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. If a trace's redirect chain in `span-buf:sr:*` exceeds 1000 hops, the loop now exits without resolving the root, `set_span_id` stays at the 1000th intermediate node, and the span is buffered under a partial key — silently splitting one segment into multiple flushed segments. This is a 10x reduction in the supported chain depth with no accompanying metric, log, or test, so the failure mode is invisible in production.

findings.title: zpopmin eviction can drop the root span, producing segments with no is_segment span
findings.body: Eviction removes the spans with the smallest end_timestamp_precise scores whenever a set exceeds 1000 members. Nothing protects the root/segment span from eviction: if the root span's end timestamp is among the 1000 smallest (possible for out-of-order or async spans), its payload is popped while the `span-buf:hrs:*` flag is still set and the segment is still flushed under the root's key. The flushed segment then contains no span with `is_segment=true`, and every remaining span is stamped with a `segment_id` referring to a span that isn't in the payload — breaking the segment contract for downstream consumers. Evicted spans are also silently dropped with no metric, so the data loss is unobservable.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now dead and disagrees with the hardcoded Lua limit
findings.body: The Python-side enforcement of `max_segment_spans` (the check in `_load_segment_data` with its `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric and error log) was removed in favor of eviction inside the Lua script, but the `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` constructor parameter was left in place and is now never read. Meanwhile the Lua script hardcodes its own limit of 1000. Consequence: any deployment that configures `max_segment_spans` via options gets silently ignored behavior, and the off-by-one (1001 vs 1000) plus the dead parameter will confuse future readers. The limit should be passed to the script (e.g., as an ARGV) or the parameter removed.
